summary: Add a client-side search box to the Teams page

checks.what: The Teams page shows a text input with placeholder 'Search teams…' directly above the team list, and all five seeded teams (Core-Platform, Design, QA-Automation, growth, Support) are listed before typing anything
Typing 'automation' into the search box leaves exactly one row, 'QA-Automation', and removes the other four team rows from the list
Typing the all-lowercase 'core-platform' still matches the mixed-case team 'Core-Platform', which remains the only visible row
Typing 'zzzz' hides the team list entirely (zero team rows) and shows the message 'No teams match your search.'
Clearing the search input brings back all five teams and removes the 'No teams match your search.' message

With 'design' typed in the search box, clicking the still-visible 'Design' row opens /teams/2/edit and that page shows the team edit card: the visible card title reads 'Edit Team "Design"' and the Team Name field (#teamtext) is present holding the value 'Design'. NOTE for the checker: stock Vikunja renders card titles as

, never

-

, so match the visible TEXT or .card-header-title rather than a semantic heading role —
on this page contains no heading elements at all and never did.
checks.where: /teams — ul.teams li a, lands on /teams/2/edit; assert main .card-header-title and #teamtext

mockHarness.notes: Dev-only Vite config + middleware mocking the Vikunja /api/v1 REST API (info, login/token refresh, user, avatar, teams CRUD) and injecting a mock JWT so the app boots already logged in; seeds five teams and returns the x-max-permission header on single-team GETs so the team edit card renders.
